newsitem.title: USA: GPU proposes Pennsylvania open market pilot.
newsitem.headline: GPU proposes Pennsylvania open market pilot.

text.p: GPU Energy said Monday it has proposed allowing about 50,000 of its Pennsylvania customers choose their own power suppliers in a pilot program that would make up to 230 megawatts of the GPU Inc subsidary's power available to the open market.
"We believe our effort is the largest retail access pilot program announced to date in the United States," said Dennis Baldassari, president of GPU Energy.
"Customers who participate will he able to choose who supplies their electricity, just as they choose who provides them with long-distance phone service," he explained.
"GPU Energy will continue to deliver the electricity to the customer over its lines, just as long distance calls are transmitted over the local phone company's wires."
In a letter to the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission previewing the program, Baldassari reviewed the scope of GPU Energy's pilot program.
The company said the following are some of the highlights of the plan:
-- The program will run for two years and will encompass residential, commercial and industrial customers.

-- Customers will be selected to participate on a random basis, with monitoring of the process by an independent auditing firm. Selected customers then will decide themselves whether they will participate.

-- Up to 230 megawatts of electricity, or five percent of GPU Energy's peak load in Pennsylvania, will be made available to the open market. This translates to about 50,000 of the one million GPU Energy customers in Pennsylvania.

-- Half of the residential customers will come from eight communities that will be selected for the pilot. All the residential and small commercial customers in those communities will be eligible. The remaining customers, including all the larger commercial and industrial customers, will be selected randomly from throughout GPU Energy's service territory in Pennsylvania.
-- There will be no charge to customers to become a participant or to end participation.
-- An extensive educational campaign will be conducted for customers on competition in electricity and on the workings of the pilot program.

"The program is another example of our efforts to bring the benefits of competition and customer choice to the Commonwealth and its citizens, and we intend to discuss with the Commission the elements of the plan, Baldassari said.
